# Phase Two — Critique and Twenty-Eight Improvements

The Awtsmoos gives Gevurah to guard ambition; Awtsmoos.com improves when breadth never becomes blindness.

1. HTML count is not public-route count; classify fixtures/templates.
2. Do not wait on huge Git status before lightweight route discovery.
3. Dirty plus active owner means audit-only.
4. Refresh prior audit claims from current runtime before acting.
5. Close Sefarim tests/browser before using it as precedent.
6. Source/test green cannot substitute for real layout verification.
7. Generic scores cannot substitute for actionable timings/resources.
8. Games need playable readiness, not DOM readiness.
9. Editors need initialized/responding workspace proof.
10. Separate site-owned console errors from extension/browser noise.
11. Separate required-resource failures from intentional optional requests.
12. Page overflow and intentional internal scrollers need distinct checks.
13. Test representative interactive pages at 200% zoom.
14. Prefer native form/disclosure/button semantics.
15. Preserve route identity; do not force identical visual styling.
16. Avoid new dependencies for cosmetic repairs.
17. Version changed static assets under the existing cache model.
18. Inspect compact server before adding `compact=true`.
19. Compare compact latency as well as bytes.
20. Inspect cache/content-encoding before merging CSS merely to reduce request count.
21. Tests should protect user-visible invariants, not obsolete DOM trivia.
22. Add new regression tests only after first source draft.
23. Recheck scoped status/claims immediately before writes.
24. Rerun sitewide matrix after every repair tranche.
25. Secret-scan before full snapshot publication.
26. Include unrelated safe work as requested, never known credentials/secrets.
27. GitHub push and production deploy are separate gates.
28. Production smoke must test representative routes, not only the last edit.

## Improved Sequence

Finish known route → classify inventory → full runtime matrix → rank with ownership → complete-file family repair → reread → focused tests → browser → performance → global rerun → next family → compact benchmark → secret/topology → full safe Git push → deploy → production smoke.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the final Phase Three safeguards and exact execution tranche, then harvest the currently running discovery/verification jobs.
